extracted.intended_audience: student reporters and journalism students learning feature/social-event news writing
extracted.subtask_description: Writing newspaper features and human-interest reports on exhibitions, entertainments, ceremonies, and social occasions that capture atmosphere, characters, and significance for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid descriptive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe costumes, scenery, lighting, music, and physical surroundings with specific, sensory detail (e.g., 'rose trees and wistaria-twined archways', 'candles glimmered, rose and fell', descriptions of chintzes, hats, velvet doublets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete visual and auditory details to recreate the scene for readers; list specifics (colors, fabrics, props, stage action) as shown repeatedly in the event accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest/emotional moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight tender, touching, or dramatic human moments that engage readers emotionally (examples: crippled children smiling and haltingly dancing; the little boy in the hospital holding a woman's hand and saying 'You and me, together').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spotlight small, intimate actions and reactions to give the story heart; include gestures, tears, smiles, and interactions that reveal character and pathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of direct quotes and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Include spoken words to convey personality and tone (e.g., Carnegie's remarks, children's lines, Jack Maclntyre's speech 'I like 'em all').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed short, telling quotations that reveal character or summarize an attitude; use dialogue for immediacy and color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming participants and notable attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: List performers, organizers, and distinguished guests to indicate the event's social significance (e.g., long lists of civic leaders, consuls, and university honorees at cathedral and commencement services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full names and affiliations for key figures to situate events in civic/institutional context; when appropriate, group lists by role (diplomats, officers, alumni).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and historical background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide background, history or reasons that give the event broader meaning (examples: Carnegie harking back to the fifth century; notes on Yale's centennial medical-school celebrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link the occasion to larger narratives, past events, or institutional milestones so readers understand significance beyond the immediate spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdote and humor in tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use light anecdote or humorous touches where fitting to enliven copy (e.g., the mock-obituary for 'S. Traw Hatt' with comic epitaphs; playful reporting of Carnegie 'practically rolled all the cakes into one big doughnut').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone to the event: social columns may employ irony, playful descriptions, or comic asides to engage readers; avoid undermining respect where solemnity is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere through sensory narration
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey atmosphere by combining sensory cues—sound, light, movement—to produce a 'spellbound' or festive effect (e.g., organ rumbles echoing, electric lights twinkling, bagpipes alternating with string orchestra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave sensory elements (music, light, movement) into narrative flow rather than listing them; use them to set pace and mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene structure and climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the report to build to a clear culminating moment (e.g., the Queen choosing the star, the final scene of the Cinderella play, the singing of the 'Volkshymne').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize details so the reader moves from setup through notable incidents to a satisfying concluding image or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative/angle-aware reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that the same incident can be reported differently in different outlets (note: the book includes two versions of the same commencement incident from different papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an angle appropriate to your publication (morning vs. evening, serious vs. entertaining) and be explicit about differences in treatment when illustrating contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit to organizers and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute credit where due to institutions or individuals responsible for the event's success (e.g., crediting the educational system for lifting little sufferers into Fairyland; naming committees and workers at a fete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge organizing bodies and volunteers; this situates the event socially and provides attribution for civic reporting.
